scope: Proposition 4.5 of the manuscript “A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture” (preprints/A-finitely-generated-counterexample-to-the-Eilenberg-Ganea-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 249 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bbc781ac6f173938), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The finite flag complex L, its nontrivial representation α : π1(L) → H, and the group G of (4.2) have the following properties. 1. G is countable, finitely generated, and residually finite, with cdZ(G) = 2 and gd(G) ≤ 3. 2. G acts freely on the integrally acyclic two-dimensional simplicial complex X of (4.5). The action has finitely many cell orbits and one vertex orbit, identified with G acting on itself on the left. 3. There is a finite generating alphabet S for G and a finite indexed list D of words trivial in G such that, for Λ = Z[G], the graph of X has edges g → gs and 0 −→ Λ(D) ∂2 − − → Λ(S) ∂1 − − → Λ aug − − − → Z −→ 0 (4.6) is exact, with ∂1(es) = s − 1 and ∂2(ez) = [z]. Here [z] is the oriented edge chain of the triangular boundary word z based at 1. In particular, the chains [z], z ∈ D, are a free Λ-basis of ker ∂1.
